title: Offbeat Beaches in India: Quiet Coasts Worth the Detour
seoTitle: Offbeat Beaches in India: Quiet Coasts Worth the Detour | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Quiet, offbeat beaches in India: Guhagar and Velas on the Konkan, Kasarkod and Maravanthe, Marari and Kappil in Kerala, Tranquebar, Talasari, Butler Bay and more.
description: A guide to offbeat beaches in India, quieter alternatives to the famous names: Guhagar, Velas and Devbagh on the Konkan, Galgibaga and Cola in Goa, Kasarkod, Maravanthe and Devbagh (Karwar) in Karnataka, Marari, Kappil and Muzhappilangad in Kerala, Tranquebar in Tamil Nadu, Yarada and Bheemili in Andhra, Talasari and Junput on the Bengal border, and remote island beaches.
dek: India's famous beaches get crowded in season. These quieter beaches trade facilities for space, and reward the extra effort.

intro: Offbeat does not mean undiscovered: most of these beaches are known to locals and a few travellers. What they share is fewer visitors, simpler facilities and a slower pace than Goa's north, Kovalam or Digha. Many have no lifeguards, so treat the sea with extra caution.
This guide lists the best quieter beaches by coast, with what makes each worth the detour and the nearest well-known base.
quickAnswer: Good offbeat beaches in India include Guhagar, Velas and Devbagh on the Konkan coast, Galgibaga and Cola in south Goa, Kasarkod and Maravanthe in Karnataka, Marari, Kappil and Muzhappilangad in Kerala, Tranquebar in Tamil Nadu, Yarada and Bheemili near Vizag, Talasari and Junput on the Bengal and Odisha border, and island beaches such as Lalaji Bay and Butler Bay in the Andamans. Most have few facilities and no lifeguards.
takeaways: The Konkan coast between Mumbai and Goa has many quiet beaches, some with Blue Flag certification.
South Goa's Galgibaga and Cola are among Goa's emptiest beaches.
Kerala's north (Kappil, Muzhappilangad) is far quieter than Kovalam and Varkala.
East coast gems such as Tranquebar, Talasari and Bheemili see few outside visitors.
Quiet beaches often have no lifeguards: swim only in calm conditions, if at all.

items.name: Guhagar and Velas, Ratnagiri
body: Guhagar is a long, clean Blue Flag beach behind a small temple town; Velas is known for turtle hatchlings in spring.

items.name: Devbagh and Vengurla, Sindhudurg
body: Devbagh sits on a spit between river and sea near Tarkarli; Vengurla is close to the Goa border.

items.name: Galgibaga and Cola, south Goa
body: Galgibaga is a turtle-nesting beach with very little development; Cola has a freshwater lagoon behind the sand.

items.name: Kasarkod and Maravanthe, Karnataka
body: Kasarkod is a clean Blue Flag beach near Honnavar; Maravanthe is the coast road between sea and river, with an empty beach beside it.

items.name: Devbagh, Karwar
body: A quiet spit at the mouth of the Kali river near Karwar, with island boat trips.

items.name: Marari, Kappil and Muzhappilangad, Kerala
body: Marari is a fishing-village beach near Alappuzha; Kappil near Bekal has a backwater behind it; Muzhappilangad near Thalassery is a drive-in beach.

items.name: Tranquebar, Tamil Nadu
body: A former Danish trading town with a fort on the sand and quiet colonial streets.

items.name: Yarada and Bheemili, Andhra Pradesh
body: Yarada is surrounded by hills below Dolphin's Nose; Bheemili, at the end of Vizag's beach road, has Dutch-era history.

items.name: Gopalpur, Odisha
body: A small colonial port town with a calm beach, far quieter than Puri.

items.name: Talasari and Junput
body: Talasari in Odisha and Junput in Bengal, near Digha, are quiet estuary beaches with red crabs and casuarinas.

items.name: Lalaji Bay, Long Island (Andamans)
body: A white beach in Middle Andaman reached by boat or forest walk.

items.name: Butler Bay, Little Andaman
body: A long, remote surf beach, a long ferry ride from Sri Vijaya Puram.

items.name: Kalipur, North Andaman
body: A turtle-nesting beach near Diglipur and Saddle Peak.

items.name: Minicoy, Lakshadweep
body: The southernmost Lakshadweep island, with Thundi beach and a tall lighthouse.

sections.heading: Tips for quiet beaches
list: Carry water, snacks and cash; there may be no shops or ATMs.
Check how you will get back, especially if you arrive by boat or on foot.
Swim only in calm conditions; most quiet beaches have no lifeguards.
Respect villages: dress modestly and keep noise down.

safety: Most offbeat beaches have no lifeguards; do not swim alone or in rough water.
Swim only at beaches with lifeguards, inside the flagged zone, and never when a red flag is up or during the monsoon.
Keep away from turtle nests and follow local volunteers' rules.
Tell someone where you are going on remote island beaches.

faqs.q: What are some offbeat beaches in India?
faqs.a: Guhagar, Velas, Galgibaga, Kasarkod, Marari, Kappil, Tranquebar, Bheemili, Talasari and Lalaji Bay.

faqs.q: Which are the least crowded beaches in Goa?
faqs.a: Galgibaga, Cola and Polem in south Goa.

faqs.q: Are offbeat beaches safe for swimming?
faqs.a: Most have no lifeguards. Swim only in calm conditions and never alone.

faqs.q: Which offbeat beach is good near Mumbai?
faqs.a: Diveagar, Shrivardhan and Guhagar are quieter than Alibaug and Kashid.

faqs.q: Which quiet beaches are near Kolkata?
faqs.a: Tajpur, Junput and Talasari near Digha, and Bakkhali.
